land.text: 'Basutoland gained its independence from the United Kingdom and became the Kingdom of Lesotho on 4 October 1966'

predecessors.note: The same territory under a new name; the basutoland dossier ends on 4 October 1966 with Lesotho as its successor. Cliopatria's 'British East Africa' shape (1961-1968) still holds the Basutoland footprint in 1967-1968, overlapping Lesotho's own shape: that row's dossier should drop it.

capitals.name: Maseru
capitals.note: 'Its capital and largest city is Maseru'; 'In 1884, the territory became a Crown colony by the name of Basutoland, with Maseru as its capital.'

correction.text: Lesotho as it stands in Cliopatria's 1967 shape, applied from independence: 'Basutoland gained its independence from the United Kingdom and became the Kingdom of Lesotho on 4 October 1966'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1967 but independence was 4 October 1966 (infobox 'Independence declared: 4 October 1966'). The land is the 1967 shape unchanged; in 1966 the basutoland dossier's shape holds until October.

31,559 km2 against the infobox 30,355 km2 (water negligible): ratio 1.04. At the project grid the shape resolves to 118 cells against 111 for the Natural Earth Lesotho outline, so it is drawn slightly generously around the country. The page says the 1869 treaty at Aliwal North 'defined the boundaries of Basutoland' and mentions no change since independence.

31,741 km2 for 1973-1975, 0.6 percent above the 1967 and 1976 shapes (31,559 km2); it resolves to the same 118 cells at the project grid, so the difference is drawing noise, not land. Nothing on the page, and no ledger event, changes Lesotho's territory in 1973; the same three-year blip appears in the Tanzania and South Africa rows.
31,559 km2 for 1976-2023, the 1967 shape again (same 118 cells); ratio 1.04 to the infobox 30,355 km2. The page reports no border change or dispute after 1966.
Same outline and area (31,559 km2) as 1976-2023; nothing on the page changes the territory in 2024.

region.text: Lesotho: 'Basutoland gained its independence from the United Kingdom and became the Kingdom of Lesotho on 4 October 1966'

ledger.note: 4 October 1966: Basutoland becomes the independent Kingdom of Lesotho. Infobox 'Independence declared: 4 October 1966'; the boundaries date from 1869: 'In 1869, the British signed a treaty at Aliwal North with the Boers that defined the boundaries of Basutoland.'

region.text: the capital and its district, where the SANDF and Botswana Defence Force were deployed; the pages do not say which districts the force held

ledger.note: 22 September 1998: South African troops enter Lesotho. 'the deployment of the South African National Defence Force (SANDF) to Lesotho on 22 September 1998'; 'Botswana Defence Force soldiers were also deployed', after the disputed May 1998 election and a rebellion in the army. The article calls it 'seven months of occupation'; the district is the researcher's reading, since the article does not say where the force held ground.

region.text: the capital and its district, where the SANDF and Botswana Defence Force were deployed; the pages do not say which districts the force held

ledger.note: May 1999: the last South African troops leave. 'The last South African troops were pulled out in May 1999 after seven months of occupation'; the Lesotho article: 'By the time the SADC forces withdrew in May 1999, much of Maseru "lay in ruins".' Confidence 2 (reviewer af-08-j): the end date is on the page, but neither page says the force held Maseru district, so the region is a reading.

wars.name: Operation Boleas (SADC intervention in Lesotho)
belligerents: Lesotho opposition parties and army mutineers

zones.text: the capital and its district, where the SANDF and Botswana Defence Force were deployed; the pages do not say which districts the force held

wars.outcome: The Lesotho government and the SADC force held Maseru; 'the opposition parties accepted an agreement where the LCD government would be restored to power', and the South African troops left in May 1999. No border changed.
wars.note: The article's infobox has no date range; the SADC force 'would remain in Lesotho until the Lesotho Defence Force was able to carry out their constitutional duties'. The Operation Boleas article says 'The central business district of the capital, Maseru, was burned down by opposition supporters'; the Lesotho page says tensions with South African troops 'resulted in fighting'.

certainty.note: The boundaries 'defined' by the 1869 Aliwal North treaty and unchanged since; the page notes no dispute (a 2010 petition called for 'the practical annexation of the country by South Africa'; the 'Conquered Territory' west of the Caledon is not mentioned on the pages opened).

notes: Lesotho's Cliopatria shapes are one outline (118 cells for 1967, 1973 and 1976) for 1967-2024 with a 0.6 percent drawing blip in 1973-1975; no page dates any change. The dossier adds the 1966 start (new keyframe) and the 1998-99 stay of SADC forces. Page conflicts on the Lesotho page: Moshoeshoe II's exile is 1987 in the body and 1990 in the infobox, so no ruler strip was written (the page gives no reign list: Moshoeshoe II, Letsie III, who 'abdicated in favour of his father in 1995'; 'Moshoeshoe II died and his son Letsie III took the throne'). The page text also dates the formation of the kingdom both 1822 and 1824. Pages that failed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conquered_Territory (url_not_found, retried once; the lands lost in 1858 and 1869, which the Lesotho page calls 'a portion of the western lowlands', could not be checked for modern claims). Not opened: the 1986 South African blockade and coup, the 1970 post-election crisis (no territorial effect). The occupation events follow the owner's side (counterpart = the occupier); the South Africa dossier should mirror them, and Botswana's token force is in the war entry only. Cliopatria's British East Africa shape overlaps Lesotho in 1967-1968 (bounding box south edge 30.70 S equals Lesotho's).
